objective: Follow-up to DISTANCE-INFO-20261117-001 and the owner's answer on A97 (distance has no direction and gives an order in which nothing is skipped): prove or refute that how often two distinctions differ (the differ count) determines every not-all-equal base, and test whether the candidate distances (differ count, bond distance, steps apart) are built from unit steps and give an order from any starting distinction. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-17 (Successful; refereed R1, confirmed with fixes, no Block): on knot trees one distance read from the allowed states does both jobs (-log_3|1 - 2d/N| = steps apart, proved). The disagreement count determines every not-all-equal base from four distinctions (proved; fails at three, one knot against none); in it betweenness is exactly a three-place constraint, a knot where its pairs are free. On the thread, a knot chain and the weave no distinction lies between two others under exact additive betweenness (A98; 9 of 9 frozen predictions held), while an order-only reading finds a local order of twelve nearest neighbours on the weave, not its own six (referee); the split is not a property of cycles. A97 narrowed, A98 partly challenged.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; A97 status set; referee hand-off; report.
title: Which distance carries a base's information, and which gives an order with nothing skipped
